bib.title: Keep CALM and Explore: Language Models for Action Generation in Text-based Games

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed; letter-spaced trajectory dumps in Figs 10, 15, 16 read but not recorded.

question: Can a language model trained on human gameplay transcripts supply a compact set of candidate actions that lets an RL agent play unseen text games without the admissible-action handicap?
hypothesis: Linguistic priors and game sense from human play, captured by a language model, can replace the handicap as an action-space reducer and generalise to unseen games.
contributions: A learning-based approach (CALM) for reducing enormous action spaces in text-based games using linguistic knowledge.
A new dataset of human gameplay transcripts (ClubFloyd), with an evaluation scheme to measure the quality of action generation.

method.summary: A GPT-2 (or bigram) language model is trained on ClubFloyd human transcripts to generate top-k action candidates from the last two observations and the last action. A DRRN agent learns Q-values over those candidates on 28 Jericho games; CALM is frozen during RL.
method.task: text-based game playing (Jericho), action-candidate generation plus RL re-ranking

datasets.name: ClubFloyd transcripts
datasets.split: GPT-2: 193,588 samples excluding Jericho games, ordered by transcript, first 90% train, last 10% validation; 50% variant 212 transcripts (94,609 samples); 20% variant 85 transcripts (38,334 samples); w/ Jericho 206,286 samples
datasets.source: ClubFloyd archive (allthingsjacq.com), crawled; used with the organiser's agreement
datasets.preprocessing: Removed meta-actions (save, restore) and observations over 256 tokens; removed chat logs, typos; expanded abbreviations (n to north); dropped actions the parser did not recognise; context (o_{t-1}, a_{t-1}, o_t); first example padded with 'You are at the start of your journey' / 'begin journey'.

datasets.name: Jericho (28 man-made games)
datasets.split: none; ClubFloyd training transcripts exclude these games

models.name: CALM (GPT-2)
models.init_from: pretrained OpenAI GPT-2 on WebText (Wolf et al. 2019 implementation)

models.name: CALM (n-gram)
models.architecture: bigram language model, Laplace smoothing, verb phrases x detected nouns

models.name: DRRN
models.architecture: separate GRU encoders for observation and action, MLP decoder for Q

other.filter: FastText admissibility predictor removes candidates predicted inadmissible

models.name: KG-A2C
models.architecture: knowledge-graph RL agent, uses admissible-action handicap

training.objective: cross-entropy over action tokens given context for CALM; TD loss for DRRN; softmax exploration policy
training.steps: DRRN: 10^6 steps total (printed '106' in the text, read as 10^6) on 8 parallel game instances
training.seeds: 5 independent seeds per game for the main results; one run for each variant in Table 3

other.n_gram_split: main text: 90/10; Appendix B.2: first 70% train, last 30% validation
other.drrn_replay: separate buffer of best-scoring trajectories (Narasimhan et al. 2015)
other.calm_frozen_in_rl: CALM is not fine-tuned during RL

inference.decoding: GPT-2: beam search, beam 40, keep top 30; n-gram: enumerate V x B_c plus 13 directional actions, at most 4 actions per object
inference.samples: top k=30 actions per unique game state; final score = average of last 100 training episodes; 5 seeds averaged
inference.prompting: context = previous observation, previous action, current observation

metrics.name: avg. norm
metrics.definition: raw score divided by game max score, averaged over 28 games

metrics.name: preca / reca / recg
metrics.definition: precision and recall of admissible actions and recall of the gold action in the top-k set along Jericho walkthroughs

eval.protocol: Final score of a run is the mean of the last 100 training episodes; mean over 5 seeds; ablations single run; no significance test.

availability.data: released with the code (stated as 'Code and data are available')

results.claim: CALM (GPT-2) reaches 9.4% average normalised score on 28 Jericho games without the handicap, versus 5.6% for NAIL.
results.setup: Jericho 28 games, CALM (GPT-2) k=30 plus DRRN, final-100-episode mean, seed average
results.table: Table 2, row avg. norm, column CALM (GPT-2)

results.claim: Relative gain over NAIL is almost 69%.
results.quote: Relatively, this represents almost a 69% improvement over NAIL.
results.note: The text says GPT-2 beats n-gram by 4.4% absolute, but Table 2 gives 9.4% vs 5.5%, a gap of 3.9; 3.8 over NAIL (5.6) is consistent.

results.claim: On 8 of 28 games CALM (GPT-2) beats both DRRN and KG-A2C, which use the admissible-action handicap.
results.quote: On 8 out of 28 games (underlined in Table 2), CALM (GPT-2) outperforms both DRRN and KG-A2C

results.claim: Handicap-assisted KG-A2C and DRRN average 10.8% and 13.0%, above CALM (GPT-2).
results.table: Table 2, row avg. norm, column DRRN

results.claim: Without pre-training (random-init GPT-2, 10 epochs) the score falls to 6.8%.
Adding 8 transcripts of the evaluation games raises the score to 10.9%, and the gains are not mainly on those games.
Action-set size k matters: k=10 gives 5.6%, k=20 9.6%, k=40 9.2%.
A random agent over CALM top-30 actions scores 1.8%.
results.quote: CALM (random agent) performs a poor score of 1.8%

results.claim: If RL fully exploited the maximum scores seen in exploration, the average would be 14.7%, above every model in Table 2.
results.metric: avg. norm of max score seen
results.setup: CALM (GPT-2) max score seen during RL (Fig 6)
results.quote: the average normalized score would be 14.7%, higher than any model in Table 2

results.claim: Per-game spread across seeds is large: zork1 30.39 (+/- 3.01), library 9.02 (+/- 5.07).
results.note: Table 5 does not say what the +/- denotes; library is 9.02 (+/- 5.07).

results.claim: Top-15 CALM actions contain around 30% of admissible actions; gold action is in the top-30 for GPT-2 in 20% more states than n-gram.
results.quote: the top k = 15 actions of CALM (GPT-2 and n-gram) are both expected to contain around 30% of all admissible actions in each walkthrough state

limits: Variant ablations (Table 3) are single runs; no significance test.
Authors: DRRN does not stably converge to the maximum scores seen; text games 'are still far from being solved'.
Authors hypothesise, without testing, that CALM beats the handicap on some games by excluding actions humans never issue.
ClubFloyd actions are noisy and non-optimal; the main text's 90/10 n-gram split conflicts with the appendix's 70/30.
Compute, hardware, batch size and DRRN hyperparameters are not stated; 2020 baselines.
